The display name in actor_display_name (a Google sign-in attempt refused with `signup disabled`) was replaced by hand at capture time; since ca32642 normalize() masks display names itself, and re-running it over this body and its valueDomains reproduces both unchanged, so that is no longer a hand edit. Set handEdited back to false once refresh-fixtures.mjs can reach a stand like this one.

auth-providers.handEditedReason: TRIMMED, not invented. Kept verbatim: both built-in methods and the github row, which carries the redirect shape the login page draws as a provider button. The generated rows were dropped rather than masked: they repeat that shape, and no-pii.test.ts refuses a raw UUID in a committed fixture. No field was edited. Re-record from a stand with a clean registry when one exists.

integration-email-test.why: RUK-290 §4. Three of this endpoint's four interesting shapes are failures, and an invented failure envelope records the author's belief about the backend rather than the backend. The path moved to /notify/email/test in b74a4536 (RUK-304); the recorded bodies are unchanged, because the route moved and the envelopes did not.
integration-email-test.handEditedReason: scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs issues GET only and refuses non-2xx, so it cannot capture a POST whose success is an empty 204 and whose useful shapes are error envelopes. Taken off the wire by hand against a locally built backend (main @ a814a01) and recorded verbatim, except the resolver IP inside probe_failed.message, masked as <IP> because no-pii.test.ts refuses a committed fixture carrying a raw IPv4 — the file documents that substitution in its own _masked field.

integration-provisioned-conflict.why: Backend 87da097: a row declared in the server's config file refuses every admin write with 409 and a message naming the config file. The admin screen shows that message as the explanation, so the three BFF write routes must pass it through intact.
integration-provisioned-conflict.handEditedReason: scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs issues GET only and refuses non-2xx, so it cannot capture a write whose only shape is an error envelope. Taken off the wire with an admin bearer against the local backend (maintmode @ e439d98) and recorded verbatim; the rows were unchanged afterwards.

invitation-accept-password.why: Accepting an invitation by setting a password. The frontend maps each refusal to its own copy by status AND code, and requires both tokens on success — so the envelopes it branches on are pinned from the wire, not from the announced contract.
invitation-accept-password.handEditedReason: scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs issues GET only and refuses non-2xx. Taken off the wire with curl against the local backend (maintmode @ 09abc73); the two tokens in the success body are masked, everything else verbatim. 403 seats_limit_exceeded and 409 conflict cannot be produced on the dev stand and are absent.

login-break-glass.why: /login/recovery signs the break-glass administrator in by password alone. The frontend requires both tokens on success and reads every refusal as one uniform answer, so both shapes are pinned from the wire.
login-break-glass.handEditedReason: scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs issues GET only and refuses non-2xx. Taken off the wire against the local backend (maintmode @ 865234f) with the dev stand's break-glass password, used with the user's permission; the two tokens are masked, everything else verbatim.

integrations.why: RUK-304: `b74a4536` turned `kind` into a category and moved the system to `name`, so the mapper's kind whitelist matched nothing and dropped every row — on a 200, with no error, while the screen rendered its static list and reported nothing configured. This fixture is what makes the next move of this shape fail in CI instead of on an administrator's screen. It must keep carrying BOTH halves of the pair, a login row's `health`, and both values of `provisioned` (backend `87da097`: config-declared login rows are `true`, API-created transports `false`) — record it against a stand whose config declares the login providers and where slack/email were created through the API.

auth-methods.handEditedReason: NOT RECORDABLE, for two independent reasons. Re-verify when the backend changes mintLinkTicket.

audit-log-integration.why: Security review S2 rework: instead of demanding a notify secret when its destination changes, the backend records the change on integration.updated (metadata.changes, with a secret named as `secrets.<key>` and no value). The audit route used to drop every integration.* row as an unknown action (docs/contract-gaps.md, RUK-297), so this pins both that the rows arrive and that a secret flag with neither side survives the mapper's no-op filter.
audit-log-integration.handEditedReason: NOT RECORDABLE yet: metadata.changes on integration.updated ships on the backend commit b4a9e73 (branch fix/integration-audit-diff), not deployed to the :9000 stand, which runs main. Transcribed from that commit: action/entity values from internal/audit/integration_action.go (entity_id = kind/name, details format) and its render test; the change list from internal/services/integration/audit_changes.go (enabled first, config fields sorted, an added key with no old side, secrets by name only); field omission from the omitempty tags in internal/app/api/public/audit/models/logs.go. Re-record once the commit is deployed. audit-log-security-events.why: RUK-297: these five actions were dropped by the audit route as unknown, so the security log never showed a password change, a reset, a provider link, a sign-in method toggle or an admin editing someone's messenger tags. This pins that every one of them reaches the client with the payload the backend really writes.
audit-log-security-events.handEditedReason: CAPTURED, not transcribed — but not by scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs, which signs in through the dev-bypass exchange and reaches the backend through a gateway; the self-host stand at :9000 has neither (its gateway exposes only the OAuth dance). Taken off the wire inside the stand's compose network (rows first captured with backend maintmode:main @ ef2ce99; re-captured 2026-10-08 against feat/audit-categories-regroup @ 84efe34 for the regrouped facet keys: the rows came back identical, only `facets` changed) with a break-glass bearer, then masked with that script's own normalize() and not edited otherwise. Every row was written by the real backend on 2026-10-08: password.changed by qa-editor changing their password on /settings/profile; password.reset through the /login reset-code flow; user.tags_changed twice by an admin in /admin/users (set, then changed + cleared — so both a one-sided and a two-sided diff are pinned); auth_method.toggled was already on the stand (the break-glass admin enabling email_otp earlier that day); provider.linked by POST /api/v1/me/providers/link/complete with a forged link code, so it is the REFUSED variant (empty actor, nil user id, failure_reason). A SUCCESSFUL link needs a real Google sign-in and was not recorded; per the backend's renderer (internal/audit/render.go providerLinkDetails, render_test.go TestRender_ProviderLinked) it differs only in details ("provider linked") and the absence of failure_reason, and names the account. ip/user_agent read <redacted-*> by name. Every facet is a number again: the old `auth` facet key, which the normaliser's sensitive-key rule masked into the string "<redacted-auth>", no longer exists on the wire.

audit-action-enum.why: RUK-297: AUDIT_ACTIONS fell five actions behind the backend and the route dropped those rows silently. audit-actions.contract.test.ts compares the UI list with this published enum, so the next new action fails CI instead of vanishing from the security log.
audit-action-enum.capturedBy: npm run fixtures:audit-actions (scripts/sync-audit-actions.mjs) — copied verbatim from the backend checkout, not from the wire: the spec is served on the backend's infra port, which no gateway exposes.

audit-log-session-revoked.why: session.revoked is the backend's record of revoking a session because a rotated refresh token was replayed past its grace window -- the only trace of a possible token theft. This pins that the row reaches the client with the replaying request's ip/user_agent, the revoked session_id and revoke_reason.
audit-log-session-revoked.handEditedReason: CAPTURED, not transcribed -- but not by scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs, which signs in through the dev-bypass exchange and reaches the backend through a gateway; the self-host stand at :9000 has neither. The row was written by the real backend (branch fix/client-ip-session-metadata @ 93896a6, image local-def3 -- the commit before the branch was rebased onto release/v0.3.1; the rebase left the session.revoked path unchanged) on 2026-10-08: qa-admin signed in from the browser, a throwaway container on the stand's edge network drove a refresh through the gateway with that session cookie, and 35s later (past the 30s grace window) replayed the pre-rotation cookie, so the BFF presented the rotated-out refresh token and reuse detection revoked the session. Taken off the wire inside the stand's compose network with a qa-admin bearer (GET /api/v1/audit/log?action=session.revoked) and passed through that script's OWN capture() pipeline, loaded from its source with fetch stubbed to the recorded body: total bucketed, rows sampled, everything masked by normalize(). Not edited after that. Set handEdited back to false once refresh-fixtures.mjs can reach a stand like this one.
